note: ObChange (TU Wien, HSR head Xtion). Built by objpose/tools/obchange/make_bop.py (every 3rd frame = 10 fps). Objects = the 11 ObChange YCB objects that are also in YCB-V (templates exist); the other 24 ObChange objects have no template here.
prompt_note: Prompts are the hand-written descriptive ones. objpose/tools/probe_bop_prompts.py was run over all 21 objects and its detector-recall winners were rejected: maximising raw proposal recall selects generic wordings ('box', 'toy can', 'black object') that fire on everything, and measured with diag_bop_ism.py on scenes 000048/000057 those produced detections for objects not in the scene (pudding_box 30/30 and power_drill 30/30 frames in a scene holding neither) while the descriptive prompts did not. Recall at the detector is not the objective; what survives the ISM is. On LM-O the same probe DID help, because there the class names mislead ('can' is a watering can) rather than over-generalise.
ism_overrides_why: Measured with diag_bop_ism.py on 30 frames each of scenes 000048 and 000057: the per-box owner election gives each box to the single object with the highest DINOv2 semantic score, and tuna_fish_can and extra_large_clamp then never receive a box (0 estimates in the 2026-09-19 12-scene batch). With it off both are detected (tuna_fish_can 30/30 frames on 000048). Same finding as LM-O: the election was tuned on 10 lab objects and does not transfer to a benchmark where several objects look alike.
